name: Men's Corporate Service Dress: navy blazer, white shirt and tie, gray trousers (blank nametag)
size_basis: Silhouette traced from images/base/male_semi_formal.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px, which makes the sleeve-to-sleeve 25.77 in (a men's 40R; the Class A coat at its true scale, make-blues-a.js, is 25.27 in). Trousers are added below the base image's cropped hem. No real garment was measured. Checked against CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.14 (PDF page 87 at 8x) with the figure's 1398 px sleeve-to-sleeve taken as the sheet's 25.12 in (55.6 px/in): the figure's crest centre is 5.53 in from the centre line (Fig 4.12, page 84: 5.37 in), the sheet's pocket and crest centre are 5.49 in from it; the sheet's silhouette, pocket top (12.38 in), crest and lapel overlaid on Fig 4.14 agree within 0.1 in. The lapel is the figure's: its peak is 5.58 in from the centre line at y 6.1 in, the lapel 3.9 in wide, its outer edge 5.35 / 4.44 / 3.97 / 2.84 in from the centre line at y 7.3 / 9.4 / 10.4 / 12.4 in. A rack of 4 miniatures at 11/16 in (2.75 in wide) centred on the pocket has its inner edge 4.12 in from the centre line, so the lapel edge crosses its top rows (1.23 in over the rack at y 7.3, 0.32 in at y 9.4) and clears it from y 10.4 down; Fig 4.12 draws the rack the same way, its top rows against the lapel edge. Moving the pocket out or narrowing the lapel enough to clear the top rows would leave Figs 4.12 and 4.14 (see DECISIONS.md DORAN5-ART-2). C1 (the blazer is the aviator shirt with the coat over it): the shirt, collar and tie in the opening are the aviator shirt's own art at the aviator's scale and in its colours, and the traced outline is pushed out (coat-fit.js) at the shoulder and down the sleeve, from 3 in to the shirt's short cuff 15.7 in down, wherever that shirt, placed with its neck arc through the V's top corners, would show beyond it, with 0.1 in of ease: the sleeve-to-sleeve is 25.77 in (was 25.12), the torso, the V, the lapels, the body below the sleeves and the hem are the traced ones.
landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h}; polygons and polylines are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box. lapel_left / lapel_right: the lapel-foreground faces (wearer's left is +x); arm_seam_left / arm_seam_right: the armhole seam from the shoulder point down to the chest; shoulder_left / shoulder_right: the top edge of the shoulder from the neck to the sleeve head

coat_fit.rule: the coat lies over the aviator shirt at the same scale: the traced outline is pushed out (base-art/coat-fit.js) at the shoulder and down the sleeve wherever the shirt, placed as shirt_in_opening says, would show beyond it

bow_tie_mount_in.note: where the black bow tie of the semi-formal lies in the aviator collar (sheet inches from the box's top left): on the centre line, 0.68 in under the front of the neck, where the collar leaves meet; the shirt's tie group is hidden then
